components.note: 一 (one) — a single horizontal stroke is the number one; 二 and 三 just add strokes, so the first three numbers are tally marks.
無 (traditional) — began as a person dancing with ornaments (same root as 舞). 'None' is a borrowed sense; 无 is an old variant of 無 and the shape does not explain it.
斤 (axe) — cutting tools, as in 新 new and 斩 chop. 所 once echoed the sound of chopping; "place" and "that which" are later borrowed uses.
艹 (grass) — the plant radical, as in 花 flower and 草 grass; it points to crops and harvest, the sense in 收获. Simplified 获 replaces 獲's left side with 艹.
犾 (dog-like part) — a variant of 犬 dog; 獲 originally meant catching game. Memory aid: grass plus a hunting dog, you bring something home.

example.hanzi: 他找了一整天，最后却一无所获。
example.pinyin: Tā zhǎole yì zhěng tiān, zuìhòu què yīwúsuǒhuò.
example.english: He searched all day but ended up with nothing to show for it.
example.fact: The 1845 Franklin Expedition set out with two ships and 129 men to chart the Northwest Passage through the Arctic and then vanished without a trace. Despite dozens of search missions spanning more than a century, the wrecks of HMS Erebus and HMS Terror were not located until 2014 and 2016 respectively, closing out one of exploration history's longest and most fruitless searches.

examples.hanzi: 我们在山上找了半天，一无所获。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zài shān shàng zhǎo le bàntiān, yì wú suǒ huò.
examples.english: We searched on the mountain for ages and got nothing.

examples.hanzi: 虽然努力了很久，他还是一无所获。
examples.pinyin: Suīrán nǔlì le hěn jiǔ, tā háishi yì wú suǒ huò.
examples.english: Although he worked hard for a long time, he still got nothing.

components.note: 土 (earth) — ground and land: 地, 场, 块; trash is thrown onto the ground.
立 (lì) is only a loose sound hint for lā.
土 (earth) — ground and land: 地, 场, 块; trash is thrown onto the ground.
及 (jí) is a near sound match (jī); same part in 吸 xī, 级 jí, 极 jí.
木 (wood) — buckets were wooden; also in 树 tree, 桌 table.
甬 (yǒng) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 通 tōng, 痛 tòng and 勇 yǒng.

example.hanzi: 请把废纸扔进垃圾桶里。
example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ fèizhǐ rēng jìn lājītǒng lǐ.
example.english: Please throw the waste paper into the trash can.
example.fact: Sweden burns so much of its household waste for district heating and electricity that it has at times imported garbage from other European countries to keep its waste-to-energy plants running at full capacity. The system has helped the country send less than 1% of household waste to landfills, among the lowest rates in the world.

examples.hanzi: 垃圾桶满了，快去倒一下。
examples.pinyin: Lājītǒng mǎn le, kuài qù dào yíxià.
examples.english: The trash can is full; go empty it quickly.

examples.hanzi: 街角放着两个分类垃圾桶。
examples.pinyin: Jiējiǎo fàng zhe liǎng gè fēnlèi lājītǒng.
examples.english: Two sorting trash bins stand at the street corner.

components.note: 刂 (knife; 刀) — marks cutting, as in 刻 carve, 划 draw, 别 separate; 删 is cutting something out.
册 (cè, bound booklet) — cutting writing out of a book: delete, as in 删除.
阝 on the left is 阜 (steps, hill) — as in 院, 阳, 阴: 除 first meant palace steps; to step away, remove.
余 (yú) is a loose sound clue for chú; 余 also in 涂 tú, 途 tú and 徐 xú.

example.hanzi: 他不小心删除了一份重要的文件。
example.pinyin: Tā bù xiǎoxīn shānchúle yí fèn zhòngyào de wénjiàn.
example.english: He accidentally deleted an important file.
example.fact: Deleting a file on most computers doesn't actually erase its data — it typically just removes the file system's pointer to that data and marks the disk space as reusable. This is why forensic recovery software can often restore a 'deleted' file, sometimes long after the fact, until the underlying disk sectors happen to be overwritten by something new.

examples.hanzi: 这条短信可以删除，不用保留。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo duǎnxìn kěyǐ shānchú, búyòng bǎoliú.
examples.english: This text message can be deleted; there's no need to keep it.

examples.hanzi: 请先删除不需要的照片，再保存。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng xiān shānchú bù xūyào de zhàopiàn, zài bǎocún.
examples.english: Please delete the photos you don't need first, then save.

components.note: 日 (sun) — 昂 is rising and proud, as in 昂贵 expensive (price high); the sun rising up high is an easy memory aid.
卬 (áng) — same sound: 昂 áng. 卬 is the old form of 昂.
贝 (shell, old money) — value and price, as in 财 wealth, 买 buy, 费 fee.

example.hanzi: 这家餐厅的菜非常昂贵。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā cāntīng de cài fēicháng ángguì.
example.english: The food at this restaurant is very expensive.
example.fact: Saffron, made from the dried stigmas of the Crocus sativus flower, is by weight one of the most expensive spices in the world. Each flower yields only three stigmas, which must be hand-picked, so it takes roughly 150 flowers to produce a single gram of saffron and about 75,000 flowers to produce a pound.

examples.hanzi: 这块手表太昂贵了，我买不起。
examples.pinyin: Zhè kuài shǒubiǎo tài ángguì le, wǒ mǎi bu qǐ.
examples.english: This watch is too expensive; I can't afford it.

examples.hanzi: 在大城市生活，房租十分昂贵。
examples.pinyin: Zài dà chéngshì shēnghuó, fángzū shífēn ángguì.
examples.english: Living in a big city, the rent is very expensive.

meanings: abbr. for 特種警察|特种警察[te4 zhong3 jing3 cha2]

components.note: 牛 (ox) — cattle and animals, as in 物 thing, 牧 herd, 牺 sacrifice: 特 first meant a bull, then special.
寺 (sì) is only a loose sound clue for tè; 寺 also in 诗 shī and 持 chí.
言 (speech) — written 讠 on the left of other characters: a warning is spoken.
敬 (jìng, respect) is a close sound clue for jǐng.

example.hanzi: 特警迅速包围了银行大楼。
example.pinyin: Tèjǐng xùnsù bāowéile yínháng dàlóu.
example.english: The SWAT team quickly surrounded the bank building.
example.fact: The Los Angeles Police Department formed the first dedicated SWAT unit in the United States in 1967, a response partly shaped by the 1965 Watts riots and a rise in armed standoffs that regular patrol officers weren't trained to handle. Credited largely to officer John Nelson and inspector Daryl Gates, the model was soon adopted by police departments across the country and, eventually, around the world.

examples.hanzi: 一队特警赶到了现场。
examples.pinyin: Yí duì tèjǐng gǎndào le xiànchǎng.
examples.english: A squad of special police arrived at the scene.

examples.hanzi: 特警队员经过严格训练。
examples.pinyin: Tèjǐng duìyuán jīngguò yángé xùnliàn.
examples.english: Special police officers go through strict training.

components.note: 癶 (two feet) — two feet stepping upward: 登 is to climb or board, as in 登山 mountain-climbing.
豆 (dòu) is only a loose sound hint; 登 dēng also sounds out 灯 dēng and 凳 dèng.
木 (tree) — wood, as in 树, 林, 桌; the older meaning was a wooden mechanism.
几 (jī) gives the exact sound; also in 饥 jī and 肌 jī.

example.hanzi: 请各位乘客准备登机。
example.pinyin: Qǐng gèwèi chéngkè zhǔnbèi dēngjī.
example.english: Please prepare to board, all passengers.
example.fact: Boarding by numbered zones, standard at most airports today, only became widespread after airlines studied boarding efficiency closely in the 2000s. Simulations found that a 'reverse pyramid' method — loading window seats first, starting from the back of the plane — could cut total boarding time by roughly a third compared to letting passengers board in no particular order.

examples.hanzi: 登机口在二十号，请尽快登机。
examples.pinyin: Dēngjīkǒu zài èrshí hào, qǐng jǐnkuài dēngjī.
examples.english: The boarding gate is number twenty; please board as soon as possible.

examples.hanzi: 我们九点开始登机。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen jiǔ diǎn kāishǐ dēngjī.
examples.english: We start boarding at nine o'clock.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — 刂 is 刀 (knife) on the right, as in 到, 别, 利; 刺 is to stab.
朿 (cì) — 朿 is a thorn and gives the sound — 刺 is cì, same syllable.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做: a person hurt. The traditional 傷 took its sound from 昜 yáng (also in 汤 and 场).

example.hanzi: 他在打斗中被刀刺伤了手臂。
example.pinyin: Tā zài dǎdòu zhōng bèi dāo cìshāngle shǒubì.
example.english: He was stabbed in the arm with a knife during the fight.
example.fact: The stonefish, found on reefs across the Indo-Pacific, delivers one of the most painful stab injuries in nature through venomous spines hidden along its back. A sting causes intense pain and swelling that can last for hours, and an effective antivenom for it wasn't developed until the 1950s.

examples.hanzi: 他的手被一根铁钉刺伤了。
examples.pinyin: Tā de shǒu bèi yì gēn tiědīng cìshāng le.
examples.english: His hand was pricked by an iron nail.

examples.hanzi: 那名男子被匕首刺伤，送进了医院。
examples.pinyin: Nà míng nánzǐ bèi bǐshǒu cìshāng, sòng jìn le yīyuàn.
examples.english: The man was stabbed with a dagger and rushed to the hospital.

components.note: 亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做: 体 is a person's body.
本 (root) — the root of a person, the body; the traditional form was 體 with 骨 (bone).
氵 (water) — marks water, as in 河, 海, 汤; 温 is warm, like lukewarm water.
昷 (wēn) gives the sound exactly: 温 wēn, also in 瘟 wēn.

example.hanzi: 医生给病人测量了体温。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng gěi bìngrén cèliángle tǐwēn.
example.english: The doctor measured the patient's body temperature.
example.fact: The commonly cited 'normal' human body temperature of 37°C (98.6°F) comes from an 1851 study by German physician Carl Reinhold August Wunderlich, based on roughly a million armpit readings. More recent research suggests average body temperature has been quietly dropping by about 0.03°C per decade since then, possibly reflecting lower rates of chronic infection and inflammation in modern populations.

examples.hanzi: 我今天有点发烧，体温三十八度。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jīntiān yǒudiǎn fāshāo, tǐwēn sānshíbā dù.
examples.english: I have a slight fever today; my temperature is thirty-eight degrees.

examples.hanzi: 进商场前要先测体温。
examples.pinyin: Jìn shāngchǎng qián yào xiān cè tǐwēn.
examples.english: You have to take your temperature before entering the mall.

components.note: 彡 (hair strokes, decoration) — patterns and appearance: 形 shape, 影 shadow, 须 beard; 彩 is colorful decoration.
采 (cǎi) sounds exactly like 彩; also in 菜 cài and 踩 cǎi.
票 (ticket) — originally flames flying up, which is why 票 gives the sound piào/piāo to 漂 and 飘 and biāo to 标; ticket is a later meaning.

example.hanzi: 他每周都会买一张彩票，希望中大奖。
example.pinyin: Tā měi zhōu dōu huì mǎi yì zhāng cǎipiào, xīwàng zhòng dà jiǎng.
example.english: He buys a lottery ticket every week, hoping to win the jackpot.
example.fact: One of the earliest recorded government-run lotteries dates to China's Han Dynasty around 200 BC, played under a game resembling keno, and its proceeds are believed to have helped fund public works including sections of the Great Wall. Lotteries later spread to Europe, where 15th-century town lotteries in the Low Countries raised money for city walls, harbors, and poor relief.

examples.hanzi: 他中了一张彩票，得了一百块。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhòng le yì zhāng cǎipiào, dé le yìbǎi kuài.
examples.english: He won a hundred yuan with a lottery ticket.

examples.hanzi: 彩票店门口排着长队。
examples.pinyin: Cǎipiào diàn ménkǒu pái zhe cháng duì.
examples.english: There is a long line outside the lottery store.

components.note: 灬 (fire) — fire and heat, as in 热 hot, 点 dot, 黑 black: light shining.
昭 (zhāo) is a close sound clue for zhào; 昭 itself means bright.
目 (eye) — looking; an eye turned on a tree 木, hence to look at, and mutually looking: "each other". 相 also gives 想 xiǎng, 箱 xiāng and 湘 xiāng.
木 (tree) — wood, as in 树, 林, 桌; the older meaning was a wooden mechanism.
几 (jī) gives the exact sound; also in 饥 jī and 肌 jī.

example.hanzi: 他带着照相机去旅行，拍了很多照片。
example.pinyin: Tā dàizhe zhàoxiàngjī qù lǚxíng, pāile hěn duō zhàopiàn.
example.english: He brought a camera on his trip and took many photos.
example.fact: The oldest surviving permanent photograph, View from the Window at Le Gras, was captured around 1826 or 1827 by French inventor Nicéphore Niépce using a camera obscura and a pewter plate coated in light-sensitive bitumen. The exposure is thought to have taken several days, and the faint image is now preserved at the University of Texas at Austin.

examples.hanzi: 这台照相机是我爸爸送给我的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tái zhàoxiàngjī shì wǒ bàba sòng gěi wǒ de.
examples.english: My dad gave me this camera.

examples.hanzi: 她用旧照相机拍了一张全家福。
examples.pinyin: Tā yòng jiù zhàoxiàngjī pāi le yì zhāng quánjiāfú.
examples.english: She took a family photo with the old camera.

components.note: 纟 (silk thread, simplified 糸) — threads and binding, as in 红, 给, 经: an agreement binds like a cord.
勺 (sháo) is a loose sound clue for yuē; 勺 also in 药 yào and 钓 diào.
珏 (two jades) — the same strings shape as in 琴 qín; 瑟 is a large zither, seen in 琴瑟 and foreign names.
大 (person) — a man with a hairpin 一 on his head, a grown man; 夫 also gives 扶 fú and 肤 fū.

example.hanzi: 约瑟夫是这个故事里最勇敢的角色。
example.pinyin: Yuēsèfū shì zhège gùshi lǐ zuì yǒnggǎn de juésè.
example.english: Joseph is the bravest character in this story.
example.fact: The 19th-century British surgeon Joseph Lister pioneered antiseptic surgery in the 1860s after reading Louis Pasteur's research on germs. By having surgeons wash their hands and sterilize instruments with carbolic acid, he sharply cut post-operative infection deaths, and the mouthwash brand Listerine was later named in his honor.

examples.hanzi: 约瑟夫是我们公司的会计。
examples.pinyin: Yuēsèfū shì wǒmen gōngsī de kuàijì.
examples.english: Joseph is our company's accountant.

examples.hanzi: 约瑟夫每天都带午饭来上班。
examples.pinyin: Yuēsèfū měi tiān dōu dài wǔfàn lái shàngbān.
examples.english: Joseph brings his lunch to work every day.

components.note: 豆 — an old stemmed serving dish, later borrowed for beans; in 豆腐 tofu, 土豆 potato.
肉 (meat) — rotting meat, with the broad cover 广 over it; 肉 also appears as ⺼ in body parts like 脸 face.
付 (fù) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 府 fǔ and 附 fù.

example.hanzi: 妈妈做的麻婆豆腐特别好吃。
example.pinyin: Māma zuò de mápó dòufu tèbié hǎochī.
example.english: The mapo tofu my mom makes is especially delicious.
example.fact: Tofu is traditionally credited to Han-dynasty China roughly 2,000 years ago, made by coagulating soy milk with a mineral salt or acid in a process chemically similar to cheesemaking. Soybeans are unusual among plant foods for containing all nine essential amino acids in meaningful amounts, which is part of why tofu has long served as a complete protein source in diets with little meat.

examples.hanzi: 我最喜欢吃煎豆腐。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuì xǐhuan chī jiān dòufu.
examples.english: I like fried tofu most.

examples.hanzi: 豆腐是用大豆做成的。
examples.pinyin: Dòufu shì yòng dàdòu zuò chéng de.
examples.english: Tofu is made from soybeans.

components.note: 回 (return) — a swirl or whirlpool drawn as nested squares: it turns around and comes back.
攵 (tap, strike) — hand with stick, as in 教, 改, 放: to gather by force or hand.
丩 (jiū) is only a loose sound clue for shōu.

example.hanzi: 这些空瓶子可以拿去回收。
example.pinyin: Zhèxiē kōng píngzi kěyǐ ná qù huíshōu.
example.english: These empty bottles can be taken to be recycled.
example.fact: Recycling aluminum is remarkably efficient: melting down used cans takes only about 5% of the energy required to produce new aluminum from raw bauxite ore. A recycled can can be back on a store shelf in as little as 60 days, which is one reason aluminum recycling rates are among the highest of any packaging material worldwide.

examples.hanzi: 旧衣服可以放进回收箱。
examples.pinyin: Jiù yīfu kěyǐ fàng jìn huíshōuxiāng.
examples.english: Old clothes can be put into the recycling box.

examples.hanzi: 这家工厂回收塑料瓶，再做成新产品。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngchǎng huíshōu sùliào píng, zài zuò chéng xīn chǎnpǐn.
examples.english: This factory recycles plastic bottles and turns them into new products.

meanings: president of a club, committee etc

components.note: 会 (meet, can) — simplified from 會, a lid on a container: bringing things together; hence meeting, then "can" (huì).
长 (long, grow) — simplified from 長, an old person with long hair. Read cháng "long" or zhǎng "to grow, elder".

example.hanzi: 他被选为学生会的会长。
example.pinyin: Tā bèi xuǎn wéi xuéshēnghuì de huìzhǎng.
example.english: He was elected president of the student union.
example.fact: The Royal Society, one of the world's oldest scientific academies, was founded in London in 1660. Isaac Newton served as its president from 1703 until his death in 1727, using the position at times to promote his own priority disputes, most notably his long-running feud with Gottfried Leibniz over who had really invented calculus.

examples.hanzi: 会长宣布会议开始。
examples.pinyin: Huìzhǎng xuānbù huìyì kāishǐ.
examples.english: The chairman announced the meeting had begun.

examples.hanzi: 我们学校的会长是一位高年级的同学。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xuéxiào de huìzhǎng shì yí wèi gāo niánjí de tóngxué.
examples.english: The president of our school society is an upper-grade student.

components.note: 心 (heart) — a picture of a heart. Written 忄 on the left (快, 怕) and 心 at the bottom (想, 思, 忘); it marks feelings and thoughts.
石 (stone) — marks stone and hard things, as in 破, 码, 砖; 碎 is to smash into bits.
卒 (zú) hints at the sound: 碎 suì is close to 醉 zuì and 翠 cuì.

example.hanzi: 得知这个消息，她感到非常心碎。
example.pinyin: Dézhī zhège xiāoxi, tā gǎndào fēicháng xīnsuì.
example.english: Upon hearing this news, she felt utterly heartbroken.
example.fact: 'Broken heart syndrome,' medically known as takotsubo cardiomyopathy, is a real, usually temporary heart condition triggered by extreme emotional or physical stress, in which a surge of stress hormones causes part of the heart muscle to weaken and bulge outward. Japanese researchers who first described it in 1990 named it after a round-bottomed octopus trap the ballooned heart resembled on a cardiac scan.

examples.hanzi: 朋友的话让我感到心碎。
examples.pinyin: Péngyou de huà ràng wǒ gǎndào xīnsuì.
examples.english: My friend's words broke my heart.

examples.hanzi: 这首歌听得人心碎。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shǒu gē tīng de rén xīnsuì.
examples.english: This song is heartbreaking to listen to.

components.note: 人 (person) — 禽 first meant to capture an animal; it now means birds, as in 家禽 poultry and 禽兽 beasts.
兽 (simplified 獸) — the old form paired a hunted animal with a dog 犬; it means beast, as in 野兽 and 怪兽.

example.hanzi: 这种残忍的行为简直如同禽兽。
example.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng cánrěn de xíngwéi jiǎnzhí rútóng qínshòu.
example.english: This kind of cruel behavior is simply beastly.
example.fact: Before Carl Linnaeus's 18th-century taxonomy sorted animals by biology rather than appearance, many naturalists grouped bats with birds simply because both fly, and some medieval bestiaries described bats as neither true bird nor true beast. Genetic evidence has since confirmed bats are placental mammals, closely related to other mammal groups and not birds at all.

examples.hanzi: 虐待动物的人简直是禽兽。
examples.pinyin: Nüèdài dòngwù de rén jiǎnzhí shì qínshòu.
examples.english: People who abuse animals are no better than beasts.

examples.hanzi: 他骂那个坏人是禽兽不如。
examples.pinyin: Tā mà nàge huàirén shì qínshòu bùrú.
examples.english: He cursed that bad guy as worse than a beast.

components.note: 氵 (water) — marks water and sinking, as in 海, 没 sink, 游; 沉 is to sink.
冗 (rǒng) is only a loose sound hint for chén.
重 (zhòng) is a sound clue for 种 zhǒng/zhòng; it means heavy (zhòng) or to repeat (chóng, as in 重新).

example.hanzi: 听到这个坏消息，他的心情十分沉重。
example.pinyin: Tīngdào zhège huài xiāoxi, tā de xīnqíng shífēn chénzhòng.
example.english: Hearing this bad news, he felt very heavy-hearted.
example.fact: Neutron stars are so dense that a single teaspoon of their material would weigh roughly a billion tons on Earth, comparable to a mountain compressed into a sugar-cube-sized volume. This extreme density results from a dying star's gravity crushing its core until protons and electrons merge into neutrons during a supernova collapse.

examples.hanzi: 这个包很沉重，我背不动。
examples.pinyin: Zhège bāo hěn chénzhòng, wǒ bēi bu dòng.
examples.english: This bag is very heavy; I can't carry it.

examples.hanzi: 老人的脚步十分沉重。
examples.pinyin: Lǎorén de jiǎobù shífēn chénzhòng.
examples.english: The old man's steps were very heavy.

components.note: 氵 (water radical, 三点水) — water and liquids: 河, 汤, 洗; 汽 is steam, water turned to vapor.
气 (qì) is the same sound, and means vapor too.
水 (water) — a picture of flowing water; as a radical it appears as 氵 on the left (海, 河) or 水 at the bottom (泉, 冰).

example.hanzi: 天气太热了，我想喝一杯冰汽水。
example.pinyin: Tiānqì tài rè le, wǒ xiǎng hē yì bēi bīng qìshuǐ.
example.english: It's so hot, I want to drink a cold soda.
example.fact: Carbonated water was first artificially produced in 1767 by English scientist Joseph Priestley, who discovered that infusing water with carbon dioxide gas collected above a beer vat created a fizzy drink. His method later inspired Johann Jacob Schweppe to found the Schweppes company in 1783, one of the earliest commercial makers of soda water.

examples.hanzi: 我口渴了，想喝一瓶汽水。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ kǒu kě le, xiǎng hē yì píng qìshuǐ.
examples.english: I'm thirsty and want to drink a bottle of soda.

examples.hanzi: 孩子们喜欢喝橙子味的汽水。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen xǐhuan hē chéngzi wèi de qìshuǐ.
examples.english: Kids like orange-flavored soda.

components.note: 夂 (foot) — stopping or going: 处 first meant to stay or settle, then a place or to deal with.
冫 (ice) — here the ice form of 氵 (water): 决 first meant to break a dam, so a decisive break.
夬 (guài) is a loose sound clue for jué; 夬 also sounds out 快 kuài and 块 kuài.

example.hanzi: 那名囚犯最终被依法处决。
example.pinyin: Nà míng qiúfàn zuìzhōng bèi yīfǎ chǔjué.
example.english: That prisoner was ultimately executed according to law.
example.fact: France adopted the guillotine in 1792 during the Revolution after physician Joseph-Ignace Guillotin championed it as a faster, more humane, and more egalitarian method of execution than the sword or axe, since it worked instantly regardless of the executioner's skill or the condemned person's social rank. It remained France's official method of execution until the country abolished capital punishment in 1981.

examples.hanzi: 那名罪犯被判处决。
examples.pinyin: Nà míng zuìfàn bèi pàn chǔjué.
examples.english: That criminal was sentenced to execution.

examples.hanzi: 古代的犯人常常会被公开处决。
examples.pinyin: Gǔdài de fànrén chángcháng huì bèi gōngkāi chǔjué.
examples.english: In ancient times, convicts were often executed in public.

components.note: 化 (change) — one person 亻 beside an upside-down person 匕 — a change of state; 化 is to change, as in 文化 and 变化.
马 (horse) — horses: 骑, 驾, 骄; 验 first meant testing a horse, then any test.
佥 (qiān) gives the -ian rhyme; same part in 险 xiǎn, 检 jiǎn, 脸 liǎn, 签 qiān.

example.hanzi: 医院对血液样本进行了化验。
example.pinyin: Yīyuàn duì xiěyè yàngběn jìnxíngle huàyàn.
example.english: The hospital ran lab tests on the blood sample.
example.fact: Modern blood typing, essential to safe laboratory testing and transfusion, was discovered by Austrian physician Karl Landsteiner around 1900, after he found that mixing blood from different people sometimes caused red cells to clump together dangerously. His ABO blood group system explained why earlier transfusions had so often proven fatal, and it earned him the 1930 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.

examples.hanzi: 医生让我去做尿液化验。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng ràng wǒ qù zuò niàoyè huàyàn.
examples.english: The doctor told me to have a urine test.

examples.hanzi: 化验结果明天可以拿到。
examples.pinyin: Huàyàn jiéguǒ míngtiān kěyǐ ná dào.
examples.english: The test results can be collected tomorrow.

components.note: 凵 (open pit) — oldest form shows a foot stepping out of a pit or cave: to go out, come out.
手 (hand) — a picture of a hand with fingers spread. As a left-hand radical it becomes 扌 in 打 hit, 拿 take, 推 push.

example.hanzi: 他这次出手很大方，请大家吃了顿好饭。
example.pinyin: Tā zhè cì chūshǒu hěn dàfang, qǐng dàjiā chīle dùn hǎo fàn.
example.english: He was very generous this time, treating everyone to a nice meal.
example.fact: Eye-tracking studies of chess grandmasters have found that when deciding a move in a critical position, they typically consider only a handful of candidate options, often fewer than five, rather than exhaustively searching every possibility. Their advantage comes largely from pattern recognition built up from tens of thousands of previously studied positions, a finding that shaped early research into the nature of human expertise.

examples.hanzi: 他出手很快，一下就接住了球。
examples.pinyin: Tā chūshǒu hěn kuài, yíxià jiù jiēzhù le qiú.
examples.english: He acted quickly and caught the ball at once.

examples.hanzi: 这次该你出手了，我们都在看着你。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì gāi nǐ chūshǒu le, wǒmen dōu zài kànzhe nǐ.
examples.english: It's your turn to make a move; we're all watching you.

components.note: 氵 (water) — liquids and flowing; 没 first meant sink or submerge (淹没), which led to "gone" and then "not have".
殳 (shū) is only a loose sound hint for 没 (méi/mò); it also sits in 设 shè and 投 tóu.
戈 (halberd) — weapons, as in 战 war and 成; the traditional 戲 was a play or contest.

example.hanzi: 这次比赛我们输定了，没戏了。
example.pinyin: Zhè cì bǐsài wǒmen shū dìng le, méixì le.
example.english: We're bound to lose this match, there's no chance.
example.fact: The 1969 New York Mets entered their Major League Baseball season at roughly 100-to-1 odds against winning the World Series, following years as one of the league's weakest teams, yet went on to win it in a run still nicknamed the 'Miracle Mets.' Bookmakers and sportswriters still cite the season as a classic caution against treating long odds as a certainty.

examples.hanzi: 这个计划被老板否决了，看来没戏了。
examples.pinyin: Zhège jìhuà bèi lǎobǎn fǒujué le, kànlái méi xì le.
examples.english: The boss rejected this plan, so it seems hopeless.

examples.hanzi: 他们俩根本不合适，我觉得没戏。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen liǎ gēnběn bù héshì, wǒ juéde méi xì.
examples.english: The two of them don't suit each other at all; I think there's no chance.

components.note: 讠 (speech, from 言) — marks talk and language, as in 说, 语, 话; 读 is to read aloud.
卖 (mài) is only a loose hint for dú; it stands in for an older 賣, as in 牍 dú and 犊 dú.
者 (zhě) is a sound clue for 都 dū, 著 zhù, 煮 zhǔ, 猪 zhū and 诸 zhū; as a word it means "one who", as in 作者 author.

example.hanzi: 这本书的读者大多是年轻人。
example.pinyin: Zhè běn shū de dúzhě dàduō shì niánqīng rén.
example.english: The readers of this book are mostly young people.
example.fact: Silent reading, taken for granted today, was apparently unusual enough in the ancient world that Saint Augustine described being astonished in the 4th century AD to see Ambrose of Milan reading a text without moving his lips or speaking the words aloud. Historians believe widespread silent reading only became common in Europe centuries later, aided by the introduction of spaces between written words and improved lighting.

examples.hanzi: 这位作家有很多忠实的读者。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi zuòjiā yǒu hěn duō zhōngshí de dúzhě.
examples.english: This writer has many loyal readers.

examples.hanzi: 读者来信说，这篇文章很有帮助。
examples.pinyin: Dúzhě láixìn shuō, zhè piān wénzhāng hěn yǒu bāngzhù.
examples.english: A reader's letter says this article is very helpful.

components.note: 亻 (person) — a person leaning to one side; also in 他 he, 们 plural.
扁 (biǎn) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 篇 piān and 遍 biàn.
離 (traditional) — 隹 (bird) plus 离 as sound (lí). 离 was an old name for a mythical beast, so the 'leave' sense comes from 離; 离 kept only the sound part.

example.hanzi: 这架飞机的航线偏离了原来的计划。
example.pinyin: Zhè jià fēijī de hángxiàn piānlíle yuánlái de jìhuà.
example.english: This plane's flight path deviated from the original plan.
example.fact: Earth's magnetic north pole is not fixed in place — it has been drifting from northern Canada toward Siberia at an accelerating pace, moving over 50 kilometers a year in recent decades. The shift has forced the World Magnetic Model, which underlies GPS navigation and compass readings worldwide, to be updated more frequently than originally planned.

examples.hanzi: 这艘船偏离了航线。
examples.pinyin: Zhè sōu chuán piānlí le hángxiàn.
examples.english: This ship has strayed from its course.

examples.hanzi: 他的想法偏离了现实。
examples.pinyin: Tā de xiǎngfǎ piānlí le xiànshí.
examples.english: His thinking has drifted away from reality.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 室 room, 安 safe, 字 character; 家 is home.
豕 (pig) — a pig under a roof: pigs were kept in the home, hence home and family.
尸 (body, building) — dwelling and body words: 居, 屋, 层; 属 is to belong to a family or group.
Traditional 屬 had 蜀 (shǔ) as sound part, also in 独 dú, 烛 zhú, 触 chù; simplified 属 keeps the reading shǔ.

example.hanzi: 医院通知了病人的家属。
example.pinyin: Yīyuàn tōngzhīle bìngrén de jiāshǔ.
example.english: The hospital notified the patient's family members.
example.fact: After the Titanic sank in 1912, compensation owed to victims' families by the White Star Line was governed by a US maritime law that capped a shipowner's liability at the salvage value of the ship's lifeboats — worth only about $91,805 total. The obvious inadequacy of that payout spurred the US Congress to reform maritime liability law in the years that followed.

examples.hanzi: 他的家属都在外地。
examples.pinyin: Tā de jiāshǔ dōu zài wàidì.
examples.english: His family members are all in other cities.

examples.hanzi: 员工家属可以免费参加活动。
examples.pinyin: Yuángōng jiāshǔ kěyǐ miǎnfèi cānjiā huódòng.
examples.english: Employees' family members can attend the event for free.

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement, as in 过, 近, 进: to go and pick.
先 (xiān) is a close sound clue for xuǎn; 先 also in 洗 xǐ.
凵 (open pit) — oldest form shows a foot stepping out of a pit or cave: to go out, come out.

example.hanzi: 全班同学投票选出了新的班长。
example.pinyin: Quán bān tóngxué tóupiào xuǎnchūle xīn de bānzhǎng.
example.english: The whole class voted to elect a new class monitor.
example.fact: Ancient Athenian democracy filled most public offices not by election but by lottery, using a stone device called a kleroterion that randomly selected citizens' tokens. The Greeks distrusted elections as prone to favor the wealthy and eloquent, and saw random selection as a better embodiment of equality among citizens.

examples.hanzi: 老师从五个人里选出了一名代表。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī cóng wǔ gè rén lǐ xuǎnchū le yì míng dàibiǎo.
examples.english: The teacher picked one representative from the five people.

examples.hanzi: 我们要选出一个最合适的名字。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào xuǎnchū yí gè zuì héshì de míngzi.
examples.english: We need to choose the most suitable name.

components.note: 钅 (metal, simplified 金) — metals, as in 钱, 铁, 错: a bell is cast metal.
中 (zhōng) gives the exact sound; 中 also means middle.
页 (head, page) — in traditional 頭 (豆 + 页): 页 is an old picture of a head, as in 顶, 领, 额. 头 dropped both parts.
大 (big) — the bottom. Memory aid: a big 大 body with two dots ⺀ like eyes above — the head, as in 头发. The dictionary's reading is loose.

example.hanzi: 开车到那里大概要两个钟头。
example.pinyin: kāichē dào nàlǐ dàgài yào liǎng gè zhōngtóu.
example.english: Driving there takes about two hours.
example.fact: The mechanical escapement clock, invented in medieval Europe around the 14th century, was one of the first machines to divide time into equal, repeatable intervals — before that, most timekeeping relied on sundials or water clocks that varied with the seasons. This standardization of the hour eventually made synchronized schedules, and later factory shift work, possible on a mass scale.

examples.hanzi: 这部电影要看两个钟头。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng yào kàn liǎng gè zhōngtóu.
examples.english: This movie takes two hours to watch.

examples.hanzi: 我等了你半个钟头了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ děng le nǐ bàn gè zhōngtóu le.
examples.english: I've been waiting for you for half an hour.

components.note: 礻 (spirit, omen) — 礻 is the ritual radical (示), as in 神, 礼, 福; misfortune was seen as a spirit's doing.
呙 (guō) — loose hint — 祸 is huò; 呙 also sounds out 过 guò and 锅 guō.

example.hanzi: 酒后开车会闯祸。
example.pinyin: Jiǔ hòu kāichē huì chuǎnghuò.
example.english: Driving after drinking will cause a disaster.
example.fact: 祸 gives 车祸 (car accident), 闯祸 (cause trouble), 祸不单行 (misfortunes never come singly) and 祸从口出 (disaster comes from the mouth).

examples.hanzi: 祸从口出，说话要小心。
examples.pinyin: Huò cóng kǒu chū, shuōhuà yào xiǎoxīn.
examples.english: Trouble comes from the mouth, so be careful what you say.

examples.hanzi: 这次车祸让他受了伤。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì chēhuò ràng tā shòu le shāng.
examples.english: This car accident left him injured.

components.note: 比 (bǐ) — near sound — 毕 is bì; 比 also sounds out 毙 bì, so the shared syllable bì is easy to remember.

example.hanzi: 他今年大学毕业。
example.pinyin: Tā jīnnián dàxué bìyè.
example.english: He's graduating from university this year.
example.fact: 毕 gives 毕业 (graduate), 毕竟 (after all), 完毕 (complete) and 毕生 (a whole lifetime). It's also a surname.

examples.hanzi: 她明年大学毕业了。
examples.pinyin: Tā míngnián dàxué bìyè le.
examples.english: She will graduate from university next year.

examples.hanzi: 会议已经结束，毕竟大家都累了。
examples.pinyin: Huìyì yǐjīng jiéshù, bìjìng dàjiā dōu lèi le.
examples.english: The meeting is over, because after all everyone was tired.

components.note: 力 (strength) — with 口 mouth: adding strength by words, hence to add, to increase. 加 also in 架 jià and 驾 jià.
亻 (person) — marks people and their actions, as in 你, 信; 倍 is doubling, as in 加倍 and 两倍.
咅 (pǒu) — only a loose sound hint (bèi vs pǒu); same part sits in 部 bù and 培 péi.

example.hanzi: 如果不小心保管，损失可能会加倍。
example.pinyin: rúguǒ bù xiǎoxīn bǎoguǎn, sǔnshī kěnéng huì jiābèi.
example.english: If it's not handled carefully, the losses could double.
example.fact: Exponential doubling is deceptively powerful: a single sheet of paper folded 42 times would theoretically reach the Moon, because each fold doubles its thickness. This is the same principle behind Moore's Law, which observed that the number of transistors on a computer chip roughly doubled every two years for decades.

examples.hanzi: 这个周末商场的所有商品都加倍优惠。
examples.pinyin: Zhège zhōumò shāngchǎng de suǒyǒu shāngpǐn dōu jiābèi yōuhuì.
examples.english: This weekend all goods in the mall come with double the discount.

examples.hanzi: 你要加倍努力，才能赶上大家。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yào jiābèi nǔlì, cái néng gǎn shàng dàjiā.
examples.english: You need to work twice as hard to catch up with everyone.

components.note: 正 (zhèng) is a close sound clue for zhěng; 正 also means correct, fitting for putting things in order.
攵 (tap, strike) — hand with stick, as in 教, 收, 改: setting things right by force.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 安, 室: a building holds things.
谷 (valley) — a hollow that holds: 容 is to hold or allow.

example.hanzi: 她决定去做整容手术改变鼻子的形状。
example.pinyin: tā juédìng qù zuò zhěngróng shǒushù gǎibiàn bízi de xíngzhuàng.
example.english: She decided to have plastic surgery to change the shape of her nose.
example.fact: The first modern techniques for reconstructive facial surgery emerged from treating soldiers' injuries in World War I, when surgeon Harold Gillies pioneered skin-graft methods at a specialized hospital in Sidcup, England. Many of today's cosmetic surgery techniques trace their lineage directly back to those wartime reconstructive innovations.

examples.hanzi: 她为了当演员，决定去整容。
examples.pinyin: Tā wèile dāng yǎnyuán, juédìng qù zhěngróng.
examples.english: She decided to have cosmetic surgery in order to become an actress.

examples.hanzi: 他整容以后，几乎没人认得出来。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhěngróng yǐhòu, jīhū méi rén rèn de chūlái.
examples.english: After his cosmetic surgery, hardly anyone could recognize him.

components.note: 酉 (wine jar) — marks wine and brewing, as in 酒, 醉 drunk, 醒; 配 first meant mixing wine, then matching.
己 (jǐ) is only a loose sound hint for pèi.
方 (square, direction) — early picture is disputed (a plough-like tool or lashed boats). Sound clue in 房 fáng, 防 fáng, 访 fǎng, 放 fàng.
亠 (lid) — the top. Memory aid: a lid over a bent shape — a square-cornered 'side' or place, as in 地方, 方法.

example.hanzi: 这家饼店的配方已经保密了三十年。
example.pinyin: zhè jiā bǐngdiàn de pèifāng yǐjīng bǎomì le sānshí nián.
example.english: This bakery's recipe has been kept secret for thirty years.
example.fact: Coca-Cola's exact syrup formula is one of the most famous trade secrets in business history — the written recipe has reportedly been locked in a vault at the World of Coca-Cola museum in Atlanta since 2011, and only a small number of executives have ever known the complete formulation.

examples.hanzi: 妈妈把这道菜的配方写在了本子上。
examples.pinyin: Māma bǎ zhè dào cài de pèifāng xiě zài le běnzi shàng.
examples.english: Mom wrote this dish's recipe in her notebook.

examples.hanzi: 这种药的配方是严格保密的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng yào de pèifāng shì yángé bǎomì de.
examples.english: The formula of this medicine is strictly confidential.

components.note: 虫 (insect) — marks insects and small creatures, as in 蚊 mosquito, 蜜 honey, 蛇 snake; 蚂 is in 蚂蚁 ant.
马 (mǎ) — same sound: 蚂 mǎ. 马 also sounds out 妈 mā and 骂 mà.
虫 (insect) — marks insects, as in 蚊 mosquito, 蛇 snake; 蚁 is the ant.
义 (yì) — close sound: 蚁 yǐ. 义 also sounds out 议 yì and 仪 yí.

example.hanzi: 一只蚂蚁能搬动比自己重很多倍的食物。
example.pinyin: yì zhī mǎyǐ néng bāndòng bǐ zìjǐ zhòng hěn duō bèi de shíwù.
example.english: A single ant can carry food many times heavier than its own body.
example.fact: Ants can collectively outweigh every wild mammal on Earth combined — a 2022 study estimated the total ant population at around 20 quadrillion individuals, with a combined dry biomass exceeding that of all wild birds and mammals put together. Their colonies also function as 'superorganisms,' coordinating complex behavior with no central leader.

examples.hanzi: 厨房里有一队蚂蚁在搬面包屑。
examples.pinyin: Chúfáng lǐ yǒu yí duì mǎyǐ zài bān miànbāoxiè.
examples.english: A line of ants is carrying bread crumbs in the kitchen.

examples.hanzi: 别把糖撒在地上，会招来蚂蚁的。
examples.pinyin: Bié bǎ táng sǎ zài dì shàng, huì zhāolái mǎyǐ de.
examples.english: Don't spill sugar on the floor; it will attract ants.

components.note: 阝 on the right is 邑 (city) — places, as in 都 capital, 邮 post, 部 part. 那 was a place name before it meant "that".
土 (earth) — ground and place, as in 地, 城, 坐: a field or open space.
昜 (yáng) is the traditional sound part, a loose clue for chǎng; the same part is in 汤 tāng, 扬 yáng and 肠 cháng.

example.hanzi: 那场雨下得特别大，街道全都被淹了。
example.pinyin: nà chǎng yǔ xià de tèbié dà, jiēdào quán dōu bèi yān le.
example.english: That rainstorm was especially heavy, and the streets were all flooded.
example.fact: The wettest 24-hour rainfall ever recorded on Earth occurred on Réunion Island in the Indian Ocean in January 1966, when tropical cyclone rainfall dumped about 1,825 millimeters — over 71 inches — of rain in a single day, more than many cities receive in a year.

examples.hanzi: 那场比赛太精彩了，我们都看得很激动。
examples.pinyin: Nà chǎng bǐsài tài jīngcǎi le, wǒmen dōu kàn de hěn jīdòng.
examples.english: That match was so exciting that we were all thrilled watching it.

examples.hanzi: 我还记得那场大雪，路上一个人也没有。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ hái jìde nà chǎng dà xuě, lù shàng yí gè rén yě méiyǒu.
examples.english: I still remember that heavy snow; there wasn't a soul on the road.

components.note: 刀 (knife) — cutting, as in 切, 刻, 到: a blade splits.
八 (eight) — originally two lines pulling apart: divide. 分 also gives 份 fèn, 粉 fěn and 纷 fēn.
攵 (tap, strike) — 攵 marks an action, here counting; as in 教, 放.
娄 (lóu) — loose hint — 数 is shù; 娄 also sounds out 楼 lóu.

example.hanzi: 他这次考试的分数比上次高了很多。
example.pinyin: tā zhè cì kǎoshì de fēnshù bǐ shàng cì gāo le hěn duō.
example.english: His score on this exam was much higher than last time.
example.fact: The practice of grading student work with a percentage score is a relatively recent invention — Yale is often credited with introducing a numerical grading scale in the 1780s, while the now-familiar A-through-F letter grade system wasn't standardized in American schools until the early 20th century.

examples.hanzi: 她的数学分数是全班最高的。
examples.pinyin: Tā de shùxué fēnshù shì quán bān zuì gāo de.
examples.english: Her math score is the highest in the class.

examples.hanzi: 你知道这次考试的分数吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zhīdào zhè cì kǎoshì de fēnshù ma?
examples.english: Do you know the score of this exam?

components.note: 臼 (jiù) — same sound: 舅 jiù. 臼 is a mortar; 舅 adds 男 (male) below: mother's brother.
男 (male) — 舅 is a male relative on the mother's side: your uncle, as in 舅舅.
臼 (jiù) — same sound: 舅 jiù. 臼 is a mortar; 舅 adds 男 (male) below: mother's brother.
男 (male) — 舅 is a male relative on the mother's side: your uncle, as in 舅舅.

example.hanzi: 我舅舅每年过年都会给我压岁钱。
example.pinyin: wǒ jiùjiu měi nián guònián dōu huì gěi wǒ yāsuìqián.
example.english: My maternal uncle gives me New Year's money every year during the holiday.
example.fact: In many matrilineal societies, such as the Mosuo of southwestern China, a mother's brother traditionally plays a larger role in raising children than the biological father does, since family lineage and property pass down through the mother's side rather than the father's.

examples.hanzi: 我舅舅在上海开了一家小饭馆。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiùjiu zài Shànghǎi kāi le yì jiā xiǎo fànguǎn.
examples.english: My uncle opened a small restaurant in Shanghai.

examples.hanzi: 周末，舅舅带我去钓鱼。
examples.pinyin: Zhōumò, jiùjiu dài wǒ qù diàoyú.
examples.english: On the weekend, my uncle took me fishing.

components.note: 亻 (person) — marks people and their actions, as in 你, 做, 住; 偷 is a person stealing.
俞 (yú) is a loose hint for tōu; 愉 yú and 输 shū share it.
手 (hand) — over 目 (eye): a hand shading the eyes to look into the distance. 目 marks seeing words, as in 眼, 睡.

example.hanzi: 弟弟趁妈妈不注意，偷看了礼物的包装。
example.pinyin: dìdi chèn māma bú zhùyì, tōukàn le lǐwù de bāozhuāng.
example.english: My little brother snuck a peek at the wrapped gift while Mom wasn't looking.
example.fact: The 'Zeigarnik effect,' named after psychologist Bluma Zeigarnik who studied it in the 1920s, describes how unfinished or hidden information — like a wrapped present — creates a persistent mental itch, making people far more likely to remember and think about it than something already fully revealed.

examples.hanzi: 他在考试的时候偷看了别人的答案。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài kǎoshì de shíhou tōukàn le biérén de dá'àn.
examples.english: He peeked at someone else's answers during the exam.

examples.hanzi: 别偷看我的日记！
examples.pinyin: Bié tōukàn wǒ de rìjì!
examples.english: Don't sneak a look at my diary!

components.note: 欠 (yawn, open mouth) — 欠 shows a person with an open mouth, as in 吹 blow, 欢 joyful; 歌 is the mouth opened in song.
哥 (gē) — same sound — 歌 is gē, just like 哥; 哥 means elder brother.
刂 (knife) — 刂 is 刀 (knife), as in 到, 别, 利; 剧 first meant to cut deeply, then intense and drama.
居 (jū) — near sound — 剧 is jù; 居 also sounds out 据 jù.

example.hanzi: 他们周末去剧院看了一场意大利歌剧。
example.pinyin: tāmen zhōumò qù jùyuàn kàn le yì chǎng Yìdàlì gējù.
example.english: They went to the theater over the weekend to watch an Italian opera.
example.fact: Opera originated in Florence, Italy, around 1600, when a group of humanist scholars and musicians called the Florentine Camerata tried to revive what they believed was ancient Greek musical drama. Their earliest surviving example, Jacopo Peri's 'Euridice,' is considered the first opera whose complete score has survived to today.

examples.hanzi: 这部歌剧的音乐非常优美。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù gējù de yīnyuè fēicháng yōuměi.
examples.english: The music of this opera is very beautiful.

examples.hanzi: 她从小就梦想成为一名歌剧演员。
examples.pinyin: Tā cóngxiǎo jiù mèngxiǎng chéngwéi yì míng gējù yǎnyuán.
examples.english: Since childhood she dreamed of becoming an opera singer.

components.note: 手 (hand) — marks hand actions, as in 拿, 打; 摩 is to rub with the hand.
麻 (má) gives the sound: 摩 mó is close, as in 魔 mó and 磨 mó.
木 (tree) — trees and wood, as in 树, 林, 本: 根 is a root.
艮 (gèn) is a close sound clue for gēn; 艮 also sounds out 跟 gēn and 很 hěn.

example.hanzi: J.P.摩根是十九世纪美国最有影响力的银行家之一。
example.pinyin: J.P. Mó gēn shì shíjiǔ shìjì Měiguó zuì yǒu yǐngxiǎnglì de yínhángjiā zhī yī.
example.english: J.P. Morgan was one of the most influential bankers in 19th-century America.
example.fact: J.P. Morgan personally organized a private bailout of the U.S. Treasury in 1895, using his own banking syndicate's gold reserves to replenish the federal government's gold supply during a financial panic — an act of private intervention in the national economy that would be almost unthinkable today.

examples.hanzi: 摩根先生是一家银行的总裁。
examples.pinyin: Mógēn xiānsheng shì yì jiā yínháng de zǒngcái.
examples.english: Mr. Morgan is the president of a bank.

examples.hanzi: 我的同事摩根下周要结婚了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de tóngshì Mógēn xià zhōu yào jiéhūn le.
examples.english: My colleague Morgan is getting married next week.

components.note: 攵 (tap, strike) — hand with stick, as in 教, 改, 放: to gather by force or hand.
丩 (jiū) is only a loose sound clue for shōu.
贝 (cowry shell, money) — money and trade: 财, 货, 买, 贵; 费 is a cost or fee.
弗 (fú) is close to fèi; same part in 沸 fèi.

example.hanzi: 这个停车场晚上十点以后不收费。
example.pinyin: zhège tíngchēchǎng wǎnshang shí diǎn yǐhòu bù shōufèi.
example.english: This parking lot doesn't charge a fee after 10 p.m.
example.fact: The world's first toll roads date back to ancient times — a stretch of road near Susa in Iran shows evidence of a toll gate from around 2700 BC, and the Roman Empire later formalized toll collection to help fund the vast network of roads connecting its territories.

examples.hanzi: 这个展览免费参观，不收费。
examples.pinyin: Zhège zhǎnlǎn miǎnfèi cānguān, bù shōufèi.
examples.english: This exhibition is free to visit and doesn't charge.

examples.hanzi: 这条路是要收费的，一次五块钱。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo lù shì yào shōufèi de, yí cì wǔ kuài qián.
examples.english: This road charges a toll of five yuan each time.

components.note: 亻 (person) — a stiff body; also in 你 you, 体 body.
畺 (jiāng) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 疆 jiāng and 缰 jiāng.
石 (stone) — marks stone and hard things, as in 破, 码, 砖; 硬 is hard.
更 (gēng) is only a loose sound hint for yìng.

example.hanzi: 长时间坐着让他的肩膀变得僵硬。
example.pinyin: cháng shíjiān zuòzhe ràng tā de jiānbǎng biàn de jiāngyìng.
example.english: Sitting for a long time made his shoulders stiff.
example.fact: Rigor mortis, the stiffening of muscles after death, is caused by a buildup of calcium ions inside muscle cells once the body stops producing ATP — the molecule that normally lets muscle fibers release their grip. It typically sets in within a few hours and fades again within one to three days as the tissue begins to break down.

examples.hanzi: 我的手冻僵了，手指很僵硬。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de shǒu dòng jiāng le, shǒuzhǐ hěn jiāngyìng.
examples.english: My hands are frozen and the fingers are stiff.

examples.hanzi: 他的态度很僵硬，一点也不愿意让步。
examples.pinyin: Tā de tàidù hěn jiāngyìng, yìdiǎn yě bú yuànyì ràngbù.
examples.english: His attitude is rigid, and he is not willing to give way at all.

components.note: 氵 (water) — water and flow, as in 河, 海, 清: 演 first meant a long flowing stream, then spreading out and performing.
寅 (yín) is a close sound clue for yǎn.
习 (practice) — simplified from 習, a young bird 羽 flapping its wings again and again to learn to fly.

example.hanzi: 学校每个学期都会安排一次消防演习。
example.pinyin: xuéxiào měi gè xuéqī dōu huì ānpái yí cì xiāofáng yǎnxí.
example.english: The school arranges a fire drill once every semester.
example.fact: The largest peacetime military exercise series during the Cold War, NATO's 'Reforger,' at times involved moving well over 100,000 troops and their equipment across the Atlantic to Europe, testing how quickly the alliance could reinforce its defenses if war broke out.

examples.hanzi: 军队正在海边进行实战演习。
examples.pinyin: Jūnduì zhèngzài hǎibiān jìnxíng shízhàn yǎnxí.
examples.english: The army is carrying out a live-fire exercise by the sea.

examples.hanzi: 我们今天下午有地震演习。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen jīntiān xiàwǔ yǒu dìzhèn yǎnxí.
examples.english: We have an earthquake drill this afternoon.

components.note: 束 (bind) — a 木 tied around with a cord 口: a bundle of wood. 束 also gives 速 sù (hurried) and 嗽 sòu.
纟 (silk thread; traditional 糸) — marks thread and tying, as in 给 give, 绑 bind; 缚 is tying up, as in 束缚.
尃 (fū) — close sound: 缚 fù. 尃 sounds out 博 bó, 簿 bù and 傅 fù.

example.hanzi: 传统观念常常束缚着人们的选择。
example.pinyin: chuántǒng guānniàn chángcháng shùfù zhe rénmen de xuǎnzé.
example.english: Traditional attitudes often constrain people's choices.
example.fact: Straitjackets, perhaps the most literal embodiment of being physically bound, were first introduced in 18th-century French asylums as an alternative to chains and were originally seen as a humane innovation — though by the 20th century they had become a symbol of the harsh restraint methods psychiatric institutions later moved away from.

examples.hanzi: 他想摆脱工作的束缚，去世界各地旅行。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎng bǎituō gōngzuò de shùfù, qù shìjiè gèdì lǚxíng.
examples.english: He wants to break free from the constraints of work and travel the world.

examples.hanzi: 孩子不应该被太多规矩束缚。
examples.pinyin: Háizi bù yīnggāi bèi tài duō guīju shùfù.
examples.english: Children shouldn't be restricted by too many rules.

components.note: 平 (píng, flat) also lends its sound to 评 píng, 苹 píng and 坪 píng.
几 (low table) — the dictionary reads the shape as a plate or stand. Origin of 凡 'all, ordinary' is debated.
丶 (dot) — a small mark inside. 凡 is the sound part of 帆 fān sail and 矾 fán alum; also in 平凡 ordinary. Memory aid: a dot on a plain table.

example.hanzi: 他过着平凡却充实的生活。
example.pinyin: tā guò zhe píngfán què chōngshí de shēnghuó.
example.english: He lives an ordinary but fulfilling life.
example.fact: The 'Blue Marble' photograph of Earth, taken by the crew of Apollo 17 in 1972, shows a small, ordinary-looking blue and white sphere against the blackness of space — yet it became one of the most reproduced images in history and helped catalyze the modern environmental movement by making the planet's fragility visible.

examples.hanzi: 他只是一个平凡的上班族。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhǐshì yí gè píngfán de shàngbānzú.
examples.english: He is just an ordinary office worker.

examples.hanzi: 平凡的日子里也有小小的幸福。
examples.pinyin: Píngfán de rìzi lǐ yě yǒu xiǎoxiǎo de xìngfú.
examples.english: There is small happiness even in ordinary days.

components.note: 氵 (water) — marks water and flowing things, as in 河, 海, 汤; 波 is a wave.
皮 (pí) is a loose hint for bō; 坡 pō and 破 pò share it.
兰 (orchid) — simplified from 蘭, which had the grass radical 艹 on top and 闌 giving the sound lán — a plant name.

example.hanzi: 肖邦是波兰最著名的作曲家之一。
example.pinyin: Xiāobāng shì Bōlán zuì zhùmíng de zuòqǔjiā zhī yī.
example.english: Chopin is one of Poland's most famous composers.
example.fact: Poland's borders have shifted dramatically over history — in the late 18th century the country was completely partitioned and erased from the map by Russia, Prussia, and Austria for 123 years, only regaining independence in 1918 after World War I.

examples.hanzi: 我们明年打算去波兰旅行。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen míngnián dǎsuàn qù Bōlán lǚxíng.
examples.english: We plan to travel to Poland next year.

examples.hanzi: 我的邻居是从波兰来的。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de línjū shì cóng Bōlán lái de.
examples.english: My neighbor came from Poland.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢; recognising something is naming it.
人 (rén) gives the exact sound, and also means "person".
口 (mouth) — speech, as in 吃, 唱, 问: voices in unison. 同 also gives sound to 铜 tóng, 桶 tǒng, 洞 dòng.

example.hanzi: 很多年轻人认同这种环保的生活方式。
example.pinyin: hěn duō niánqīngrén rèntóng zhè zhǒng huánbǎo de shēnghuó fāngshì.
example.english: Many young people identify with this eco-friendly lifestyle.
example.fact: Social identity theory, developed by psychologist Henri Tajfel in the 1970s, showed that people form group loyalties and self-esteem around group membership so readily that even arbitrary, meaningless group labels assigned in an experiment were enough to trigger favoritism toward one's own group.

examples.hanzi: 我认同你的观点，我们就这么办吧。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ rèntóng nǐ de guāndiǎn, wǒmen jiù zhème bàn ba.
examples.english: I agree with your view; let's do it that way.

examples.hanzi: 他很难认同这个新规定。
examples.pinyin: Tā hěn nán rèntóng zhège xīn guīdìng.
examples.english: It's hard for him to accept this new rule.

components.note: 辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads: 过, 进, 送; 达 is to get through to, to reach.
大 (dà) is only a loose stand-in for the old sound part, so treat it as a rough clue for dá.
扌 (hand) — marks actions done by hand, as in 打, 推, 拿; 拉 is to pull.
立 (lì) hints at the sound: 拉 lā is close, as in 垃 lā.
斤 (axe) — the original idea was chopping with an axe, as in 新, 斩 chop, 断 break; today 斯 is mostly a sound-borrowing syllable sī in foreign names like 俄罗斯.

example.hanzi: 肯尼迪总统是在达拉斯遇刺的。
example.pinyin: Kěnnídí zǒngtǒng shì zài Dálāsī yùcì de.
example.english: President Kennedy was assassinated in Dallas.
example.fact: Dallas grew from a small trading post founded in 1841 on the Trinity River into one of the largest US metro areas largely because of oil — the 1930 discovery of the vast East Texas Oil Field turned the region into a banking and business hub for the entire industry almost overnight.

examples.hanzi: 他下个月要搬到达拉斯去工作。
examples.pinyin: Tā xià gè yuè yào bān dào Dálāsī qù gōngzuò.
examples.english: He is moving to Dallas for work next month.

examples.hanzi: 达拉斯的夏天特别热。
examples.pinyin: Dálāsī de xiàtiān tèbié rè.
examples.english: Summers in Dallas are especially hot.

components.note: 火 (fire) — cooked to mush, then rotten; also in 烧 burn, 灯 lamp.
兰 (lán) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 栏 lán and 拦 lán.
扌 (hand, 提手旁) — marks hand actions, as in 打 hit, 推 push, 拉 pull; 摊 is spreading out with the hands, then a stall.
难 (nán) — sound hint is loose (tān vs nán); same part in 瘫 tān, 滩 tān.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 新经理接手了一个烂摊子，花了半年才理清。
example.pinyin: xīn jīnglǐ jiēshǒu le yí gè làntānzi, huā le bàn nián cái lǐqīng.
example.english: The new manager inherited a total mess and took half a year to sort it out.
example.fact: The Chernobyl nuclear disaster left behind one of the most literal 'shambles' in industrial history — the surrounding Exclusion Zone remains largely uninhabited decades later, though it has unexpectedly become a haven for wildlife like wolves and lynx, since the absence of humans has outweighed the radiation's harm to many species.

examples.hanzi: 别把这件事搞成一个烂摊子。
examples.pinyin: Bié bǎ zhè jiàn shì gǎo chéng yí gè làntānzi.
examples.english: Don't turn this matter into a mess.

examples.hanzi: 这个烂摊子谁来收拾？
examples.pinyin: Zhège làntānzi shéi lái shōushi?
examples.english: Who is going to clean up this mess?

components.note: 玉 (jade) — jade put away safely: 全 first meant flawless, pure, then whole.
力 (strength) — an old picture of an arm or a plough, a tool of effort. As a radical it marks strength: 办, 助, 动, 努, 男.
人 (person) — the right-hand part. The left part is a hook-and-dot, from an old tool-like shape. Meaning 'by means of, so as to' is not shown by the parts today.
Memory aid: a person 人 using a tool to get something done — 'by means of' (可以, 所以, 以前). A mnemonic, not proven etymology.
走 (walk) — marks walking and going, as in 起 rise, 超 surpass; 赴 is going toward a place, as in 赴约 keep an appointment.
卜 (bǔ) — only a loose sound hint (fù vs bǔ).

example.hanzi: 为了这次比赛，队员们全力以赴地训练了三个月。
example.pinyin: wèile zhè cì bǐsài, duìyuánmen quánlì yǐ fù de xùnliàn le sān gè yuè.
example.english: For this competition, the team members trained with everything they had for three months.
example.fact: Free-diver Herbert Nitsch set the current 'no limits' depth record by descending to 214 meters on a single breath in 2007 — a feat requiring total physical and mental commitment, since a diver at that depth experiences pressure over 20 times greater than at the surface.

examples.hanzi: 我们必须全力以赴，不能放弃。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen bìxū quánlì-yǐfù, bù néng fàngqì.
examples.english: We must go all out and cannot give up.

examples.hanzi: 他全力以赴地准备明天的考试。
examples.pinyin: Tā quánlì-yǐfù de zhǔnbèi míngtiān de kǎoshì.
examples.english: He is preparing for tomorrow's exam with all his effort.

components.note: 木 (tree) — marks trees, as in 树, 桃; 樱 is the cherry tree and its blossom.
婴 (yīng) — same sound: 樱 yīng. 婴 also sounds out 缨 yīng.
木 (tree) — marks trees, as in 树, 林; 桃 is the peach tree.
兆 (zhào) — loose sound hint (táo vs zhào); same part in 跳 tiào, 挑 tiāo and 逃 táo.

example.hanzi: 春天的时候，果园里的樱桃树开满了花。
example.pinyin: chūntiān de shíhou, guǒyuán lǐ de yīngtáo shù kāi mǎn le huā.
example.english: In spring, the cherry trees in the orchard are covered in blossoms.
example.fact: Japan's famous cherry blossom season is driven almost entirely by ornamental varieties bred for their flowers, not their fruit — most decorative sakura trees produce little or no edible cherries, while the cherries sold for eating come from a different set of cultivated varieties bred specifically for fruit production.

examples.hanzi: 这盘樱桃又大又甜。
examples.pinyin: Zhè pán yīngtáo yòu dà yòu tián.
examples.english: This plate of cherries is big and sweet.

examples.hanzi: 蛋糕上放了几颗红樱桃。
examples.pinyin: Dàngāo shàng fàng le jǐ kē hóng yīngtáo.
examples.english: A few red cherries are placed on the cake.
